chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musafir, who said:

Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he was taken away (to be imprisoned), commanded Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) to sleep at his door every night for as long as he was alive, until his news would come to him.

He (Musafir) said: Every night we would spread a bed for Abu al-Hasan in the corridor, then he would come after the Isha prayer and sleep. When morning came, he would leave to his house. He said: He continued in this state for four years.

Then when it was one of the nights, he was delayed from us, and the bed had been spread for him but he did not come as he used to. The household became apprehensive and frightened, and a great matter befell us due to his delay. When it was the next morning, he came to the house and entered to the family and went to Umm Ahmad and said to her: 'Bring what my father entrusted to you.' She shrieked and slapped her face and tore her collar and said: 'By Allah, my Master has died!'

He stopped her and said to her: 'Do not speak of anything nor make it known until the news reaches the governor.' Then she brought out to him a chest and two thousand dinars, or four thousand dinars, and handed all of that over to him alone, not to others. And she said: 'He had said to me privately' — and she was beloved in his presence — 'Guard this trust with you and do not inform anyone of it until I die. Then when I pass away, whoever from my children comes to you and asks for it, hand it over to him, and know that I have died.' 'And by Allah, the sign of my Master has come to me.'

So he took possession of that from her and commanded all of them to keep silent until the news arrived, and he left. He did not return to anything of the overnight sleeping as he used to do. And it was not long — only a few days — until there came the sealed letter with news of his passing. So we counted the days and examined the time, and it was so that he had died at the very moment when Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did what he did — staying away from the nightly sleeping and taking possession of what he took.

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim — the honorific title of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS), the seventh Imam
key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan — the honorific title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Imam
key_terms.الْخَرِيطَةُ: Sealed letter/dispatch — an official communication, here bearing news of the Imam's death
key_terms.الْعَلَامَةُ: Sign/proof — the pre-arranged signal confirming the death of the Imam and the legitimacy of succession
key_terms.الْوَدِيعَةُ: Trust/deposit — property entrusted for safekeeping, here transferred as a sign of succession

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ridha know of his father's death before official news arrived?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Imam Ali al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Imam, supernaturally knew the exact moment of his father Imam Musa al-Kadhim's (AS) death in Abbasid imprisonment. Imam al-Kadhim had prophetically arranged beforehand that al-Ridha would sleep at his door nightly; when al-Ridha stopped sleeping there and claimed the entrusted trust, the household understood the seventh Imam had passed away — confirmed only days later when the official letter arrived. This account demonstrates the Imams' divinely granted knowledge ('ilm al-ladunni) of events beyond normal perception, a key doctrine in Shia theology regarding the Imamate.
word_analysis: with the news of his death
